names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 19 Μαΐου, «Όσιος Ιγνάτιος», with the rank word left off; the life page adds that his name in the world was Ιωάννης.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 19. мај ст. ст., „Свети кнез Јован Вологодски.“ — Свети is not a rank and кнез is the `prince` this batch adds to `types`; strip them and the fullest form the calendar gives is left. **This folder is displayed as Ignatius and the form stored for it is John of Vologda, and that is deliberate.** BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §6 allows **one `sr` form per folder, the fullest the calendar gives**, and the calendar gives the princely name in its heading while the monastic name stands in the body’s last clause, „доби име Игњатије“. **«Јован Вологодски» is the fuller of the two and is the one stored; «Игњатије» is recorded in this note and not as a second form.** This is the inverse of the «Кирил (Константин)» case the brief settles — there the name in the world stood in a parenthesis beside the stored one, here the name in the world is the heading and the monastic name is in the body — and **swapping the two is one commit if the author prefers the folder’s own name.** Measured before drafting with `foldchk.py`: «Јован Вологодски» and «Игњатије» are both held by no folder in any language, while a bare «Јован» is held by eight — so keeping Вологодски also keeps this folder out of that fold.

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 19 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and gives him two sentences. He is none of the corpus's eleven men of this name: it keeps no Ignatius who was a Russian prince's son of the late fifteenth century, and the nearest by date, `ignatius-of-mariupol` and the twentieth-century monk-martyrs, are other men. The page gives him no monastery, no place and no hymn, and the display name carries the day because the page gives nothing else to distinguish him by.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 01.06.2026 (19. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети кнез Јован Вологодски.“

attestations.note: The day’s third entry, on the same menologion 19/5 the Greek row already carries, and **the same man beyond doubt**: saint.gr’s two sentences say he was called **John in the world**, was born in Russia in **1477** the son of the prince Andrew Vasilyevich and of Helen, and was tonsured a monk with the name **Ignatius**, its head line closing him in **1522**. This entry heads him „Свети кнез Јован Вологодски.“ and closes „Пред смрт се замонаши Јован и доби име Игњатије.“ — the same John, the same Ignatius, the same tonsure. **THE PLACE AND THE IDENTITY ARE THIS BOOK’S GIFT, AND THE DISPLAY NAME IS THE AUTHOR’S.** The folder is called **„Ignatius (19 May)“**, a name chosen because saint.gr gave nothing to distinguish him by; this entry gives **Вологодски**, of Vologda, and **кнез**, prince, in his own right rather than as a prince’s son. **`upgrade.py` has no `display_name` key** and the English display name is one of the nine things `docs/CORPUS.md` §10 reserves, so nothing was renamed: **„Ignatius of Vologda“ is a one-line commit the author can make on this reading.** **THE SAME NUMBER, THIRTY-TWO, READ TWO DIFFERENT WAYS BY TWO BOOKS — AND NEITHER IS WRITTEN.** saint.gr: „At the age of thirty-two he left the world and was tonsured a monk with the name Ignatius.“ The Prologue: „одмалена он би … вргнут у тамницу … где проведоше пуне тридесет две године“ and the tonsure „пред смрт“, before his death. **One book makes thirty-two his age at the tonsure, the other the length of the imprisonment with the tonsure at the end of his life**, and 1477 + 32 = 1509 against a death in 1522. **Nothing is derived from either**: `dates` is untouched, `birth` 1477 and `death` 1522 both stand as saint.gr gave them, and a duration is not a date — the same refusal made of Pachomius’s seventy-four years on 15 May and of Christina’s sixteen on 18 May. **Which reading of the thirty-two is right is the author’s**, and the Prologue’s is the one that fits a death in 1522. **TWO `types` WORDS ADDED, NEITHER OF THEM CHANGING WHAT IS PRINTED.** „Свети кнез“ gives `prince` by BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §5 — Кнез → prince — and the entry’s whole second line, „Чудотворац.“, is the Чудотворац that §5 maps to `wonderworker`, standing alone as a title and not as a wonder narrated. **Both are absent from `PRECEDENCE` in `src/lib/honorific.js`**, so `venerable` still composes the rank over him and the two words reach the reader only in the saint page’s facts line. **New besides**: that he was **God-fearing and devout**; that **his own uncle, the prince John Vasilyevich, threw him into prison from his early years**; and that **his brother Dimitry was shut up with him for the whole thirty-two years**. **Neither the uncle nor the brother gains a folder or a row**: no calendar read for this corpus keeps either, and by the coordinator’s third ruling nothing is minted for them — they are in the prose, unlinked. No `locations`, although Vologda is now named. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
